Common Approaches Used to Evaluate
MGPs in EES
Most common approaches pursued by
districts and states using MGPs in educator
evaluations or for school accountability
discussed in last meeting:
Option 1 - Fixed (i.e., MGP based) cuts
Option 2 - Adding confidence intervals
around the median SGP or building them
into the cuts (margin of error)

Examples of both options from 3
different places
• Option 1 - Fixed MGPs: New Jersey

• Option 2A – Confidence intervals around
the median SGP: Denver Public Schools

• Option 2B – Building the margin of error
into the cuts: Rhode Island

Option 1: New Jersey
• Set up standard setting panels consisting of
teachers in different districts
• Panels Reviewed:
a. MGP distributions across schools in the
district
b. MGP distributions across classrooms in
the state
c. Performance profiles of students with
different SGP levels

New Jersey
• Panel used performance profiles to identify cuts
that would recognize different levels of MGP
growth.
• First established consensus on what classified
low, typical or high growth
• Also set one more cut to differentiate lower
levels of typical growth from higher levels of
typical growth
• Translated MGP values from 1-99 scale to the
1-4 rating scale

Other sources consulted
• In addition to reviewing their own data, NJ
DOE consulted with other states using a
similar fixed approach
• Consulted with the TAC to develop the scale

Note: Have already communicated to
teachers and administrators that cuts set
could be adjusted in future years based on
emerging information and best practices
Points assigned to MGPs in NJ

Option 2A: Denver Public Schools
Like NJ DOE, groups assembled to review
growth data and agreed to define cuts
that establish thresholds for:
a.Low Growth – below 40th percentile
b.Typical Growth – 40th to below the 60th
percentile
c.High Growth – 60th percentile and above

Computed Confidence Intervals (CI) around
a Teacher MGP

Evaluating growth with CIs
• Look at MGP in each content area
• The lower limit of CI in each content area
• The upper limit of CIs in each content area
• Evaluate these points relative to the cut-
points used to classify 3 different levels of
growth
• Teacher can earn 5 levels of growth
classified as A (lowest)to E (highest level of
growth)

Option 2B: Rhode Island
• Rhode Island initially wished to not use a
confidence interval
• Considerations of imprecision in the
median SGPs led to a desire to build in
some measure of confidence
• The state decided on using an overall
confidence interval as opposed to using
teacher specific confidence intervals

Option 2B: Rhode Island
• Note different length caterpillar “legs”. These
are the teacher specific CSEMs.
• The median SGP aggregates across both content
areas.
• With 1 standard error, there is 84% certainty
that the median SGP is actually below 35. The
“average” standard error is approximately 5
• Rhode Island built this imprecision into the
overall cut (now 30, instead of 35), with the
goal of simplifying explanation.

Take-away points from case studies
In options 1, 2a, 2b:
• Growth discussions are focused on classifying
levels of growth taking place in classrooms
• Evaluations based on criterion-referenced
definitions of growth (the cuts used) baked into
the MGP distribution
• Review of data always used to help inform the
placement of cuts
• Classifications of growth made with stakeholder
groups involved

Guiding questions

growth expectations set in your system?
